_about: RATIFIED Company Standard for LIABILITY-TOS-001 — the TERMS OF SERVICE liability
position. This is the organization's own position, confirmed by the owner on
2026-08-18 and re-scoped to document type TOS by owner decision Q3=B on 2026-08-19
(per-type standards). THE VALUE IS UNCHANGED from the 2026-08-18 ratification:
12 months of total fees. Only the scope label was added.
Formerly LIABILITY-001.json, when one global standard was assumed. Under Q3=B each
document type carries the position its own document states, so the MSA position
lives separately in LIABILITY-MSA-001.json (6 months, affected-service fees).
It is CONFIGURATION, not specification: no all_lock.md entry, no locked decision
amended. Single source of truth: corpus fixtures reference it by
`company_standard_ref` rather than repeating the values.
AUTHORITY, as the owner states it:
'This comes from the stakeholder-confirmed C-01 resolution.' The owner's
attribution governs and is recorded as given.
Corroborating fact: the 12-month / total-fees position appears textually in the
Leapswitch Networks Terms of Service (26 February 2026) section 13, second bullet.
WHAT THIS FILE DOES NOT CONTAIN, deliberately:
No acceptable_max, no approval_required_above, no unlimited_outcome, and no
Legal Rule of any kind. None is approved (owner, 2026-08-18). A deviation is
therefore NEVER automatically acceptable, approval-requiring or unacceptable:
rule_outcome stays NOT_APPLICABLE (locked Step 20 r4) and the Evaluation is
routed to a human -- see UNRULED_DEVIATION_REQUIRES_DECISION in
legalmind/evaluation/workflow.py.
source_document: Leapswitch Networks Terms of Service (26 February 2026)
source_quote: LEAPSWITCH'S TOTAL AGGREGATE LIABILITY TO YOU FOR ALL CLAIMS ARISING OUT OF OR IN CONNECTION WITH THESE TERMS OR THE SERVICES SHALL NOT EXCEED THE TOTAL FEES PAID BY YOU TO LEAPSWITCH DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM.
_semantics: unit MONTHS with preferred 12 encodes the LOOKBACK WINDOW the clause states
('the total fees paid ... DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS immediately preceding
the event'). It is NOT a multiplier of a monthly fee. The two coincide under
steady monthly billing and diverge under annual prepayment; this was reported
to the owner on 2026-08-18 and the clause's own wording was kept.
basis FEES_PAID means TOTAL fees paid, unrestricted as to which Services.
It is deliberately distinct from FEES_PAID_FOR_AFFECTED_SERVICES, the basis
used by MSA 17.2 ('for the specific Services giving rise to the claim').
45B.4 forbids assuming the two are equivalent, so a 6-month affected-services
cap does NOT evaluate as a deviation from this standard — it fails closed as
UNABLE_TO_EVALUATE. Declaring them comparable would be a legal judgement and
_owner_rulings: FEES_PAID_FOR_AFFECTED_SERVICES DISTINCT. The owner declined to declare them
comparable. Consequence, accepted deliberately: a counterparty cap measured on
fees for the affected Services only is NEVER compared numerically to this
standard — it yields UNABLE_TO_EVALUATE and goes to human Legal review, however
close the numbers look. This is 45B.4's default, so `comparable_bases` stays
empty and NO code change was needed; STD-LIAB-02 pins the behaviour.
Do not add FEES_PAID_FOR_AFFECTED_SERVICES to comparable_bases, and do not add a
conversion rule between the two, without a new owner ruling. Either would assert
that a narrower measure equals a broader one, which usually understates exposure.
_no_legal_rule: SUPERSEDED 2026-08-19 by the manager's ZERO-TOLERANCE ruling: MATCH ->
ACCEPTABLE; any DEVIATION -> UNACCEPTABLE -> Legal Decision required; no
deviation is ever auto-approved. There are deliberately NO thresholds and NO
tolerance bands -- do not add acceptable_max or approval_required_above, and
do not ask the owner for them; the policy is that none exists.
The zero-tolerance label is not yet wired into the engine (needs a
deviation_outcome config key; the threshold keys cannot express it). Routing
is already correct: every deviation reaches a human via D-3.5(a) or
UNRULED_DEVIATION_REQUIRES_DECISION, so nothing is auto-approved today either.
